# `__DS0PrimaryShowAllCompat` in Auto-Generated DAX

The `__DS0PrimaryShowAllCompat` block in Power BI's auto-generated DAX is the signature footprint of the **"Show items with no data"** setting — and a clear performance red flag when seen in DAX Studio.

## What It Looks Like

Power BI generates this block automatically inside the query when "Show items with no data" is enabled on any grouping field:

```dax
-- Simplified representation of the generated pattern:
FILTER (
    GENERATEALL (
        SUMMARIZECOLUMNS ( ...grouping fields... ),
        SUMMARIZECOLUMNS ( ...other fields... )
    ),
    OR(
        NOT(ISBLANK([Measure1])),
        OR(
            NOT(ISBLANK([Measure2])),
            OR(...)
        )
    )
)
```

`GENERATEALL` replaces `GENERATE` (inner join semantics), producing a Cartesian product of all category combinations rather than only those with matching data.

## What It Signals

When you see `__DS0PrimaryShowAllCompat` in the DAX Studio Query Plan or All Queries tab:
- Power BI is generating **every possible combination** of category values
- Cross-joins are being performed across all grouping fields
- Each measure is evaluated against every combination
- The DAX is not handwritten — it is auto-generated by the visual

## Why Reading the Generated DAX Matters

Performance Analyzer gives you timing metrics but not root cause. DAX Studio Server Timings show Formula Engine vs Storage Engine distribution. The generated DAX query itself reveals the **specific auto-generated pattern** causing the bottleneck.

In this case study: the developer noticed `__DS0PrimaryShowAllCompat` in the raw DAX query, identified the setting, disabled it, and achieved a 63% speed improvement.
